subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 100 easy / 0 medium / 0 hard. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: The minimum number of antenatal visits recommended for a normal pregnancy in India is:
questions.explanation: Visits: first within 12 weeks, then at 14–26, 28–34 and 36 weeks to term.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Which exercise best helps prevent deep vein thrombosis after surgery?

options.D: Ankle pumps (active ankle dorsiflexion and plantar flexion)

questions.explanation: Calf muscle pump activity increases venous return; combined with early mobilisation and stockings.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The Bobath (NDT) approach for stroke emphasises:

options.A: Normal movement patterns, tone normalisation and handling to facilitate postural control

questions.explanation: Bobath uses key points of control and facilitation to promote normal postural reactions and movement quality.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: According to the rule of nines, the percentage of total body surface area of ONE adult lower limb is:
questions.explanation: Adult: head 9, each arm 9, chest 18, back 18, each leg 18, perineum 1. A child has a proportionally larger head.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which spinal curves are primary (present at birth)?
questions.explanation: Secondary curves (cervical and lumbar lordosis) develop with head control and sitting/walking.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: To avoid the reactive vasodilatation phase, a standard ice pack application is usually limited to:
questions.explanation: 10–15 minutes reduces tissue temperature effectively; longer exposure risks nerve injury and tissue damage.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In a lateral view of normal standing posture the plumb line passes through the:

options.A: Lobe of the ear, acromion, greater trochanter and just anterior to the lateral malleolus

questions.explanation: Kendall's ideal alignment passes just in front of the lateral malleolus, slightly posterior to the patella centre, through the greater trochanter and acromion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Visual input from the eyes is primarily processed in which lobe of the cerebral cortex?
questions.explanation: Visual input travels to the primary visual sensory area located in the occipital lobe, at the back of the cerebrum, where it is initially processed before being passed to visual association areas.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Forebrain: Cerebrum, Sensory and Motor Functions
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: Varicose veins are caused by:

options.A: Incompetent venous valves leading to reflux and venous hypertension

questions.explanation: Great saphenous vein incompetence at the saphenofemoral junction is the commonest.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: When the velocity of a limb movement is held constant by a rate-controlling device during exercise, this is referred to as:
questions.explanation: An isokinetic contraction is one where the velocity of limb movement is held constant by a rate-controlling device (an isokinetic dynamometer), distinguishing it from standard dynamic (isotonic) exercise where velocity is not controlled.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 6: Resistance Exercise — Type of Muscle Contraction
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A greenstick fracture occurs most commonly in:
questions.explanation: Immature bone is more flexible; it bends and cracks on one side while the other cortex stays intact.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which rotator cuff muscle is the main lateral rotator together with teres minor?
questions.explanation: Subscapularis medially rotates; supraspinatus initiates abduction.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A paraffin wax bath is particularly suitable for:

options.A: Deep heating of the hip joint
options.D: Painful stiff small joints of the hands in rheumatoid arthritis

questions.explanation: Wax gives comfortable conductive heat in a layered glove over irregular surfaces such as the hand, relieving pain and stiffness; it is contraindicated over open wounds and in impaired sensation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The instrument used to measure the intensity of current in a circuit is a/an:
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures current and has very low resistance, so it is connected in series. A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which clinical subtype of OCD, involving obsessions about contamination with dirt or germs and repeated hand/body washing, is described as the commonest type?
questions.explanation: 'Washers' is the most common OCD syndrome, involving obsessions of contamination (dirt, germs, body excretions) with compensatory compulsive washing of hands, body, clothes, or surroundings that gradually spreads to more and more objects/situations.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: In a first-class lever the:

options.A: Axis is always at the end
options.B: Resistance lies between the axis and effort
options.C: Effort lies between the axis and resistance
options.D: Axis lies between the effort and the resistance

questions.explanation: Example: neck extension by posterior neck muscles (head on atlanto-occipital joint); a see-saw.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Kneading, wringing and rolling are all variations of:
questions.explanation: Petrissage is compression of muscle to improve circulation and release adhesions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A laser beam is characterised by being:
questions.explanation: The three classical properties of laser light: single wavelength (monochromatic), in-phase waves (coherent) and non-divergent (collimated).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Cryotherapy is contraindicated in:

options.C: Raynaud's disease and cold hypersensitivity (cold urticaria)

questions.explanation: Cold may provoke vasospasm in Raynaud's disease and release of histamine in cold urticaria; avoid it also in impaired sensation and arterial insufficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A good starting position for general relaxation in the clinic is:

options.A: Prone with the head rotated fully
options.B: Sitting forward on a hard chair
options.D: Supine or crook lying with support under the head and knees

questions.explanation: Comfortable, supported postures reduce unwanted muscle activity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Prepatellar bursitis is commonly known by which occupational nickname?
questions.explanation: Prepatellar bursitis is commonly called 'housemaid's knee' (or miner's knee), from repeated kneeling pressure directly on the kneecap. Subcutaneous infrapatellar bursitis, by contrast, is called 'clergyman's knee'.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Lower Limb
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The most common mechanism of injury to the anterior talofibular ligament is:
questions.explanation: ATFL is the first lateral ligament to tear in a plantar-flexed, inverted ankle. The calcaneofibular ligament is injured next.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The acronym TORCH, used for a group of congenital infections with overlapping symptoms, stands for Toxoplasma, Others, Rubella, Cytomegalovirus, and:
questions.explanation: TORCH stands for Toxoplasma, Others (hepatitis B, coxsackievirus B, mumps, poliovirus), Rubella, Cytomegalovirus, and Herpes simplex virus — a group of infections tested together in suspected congenital infection because their symptoms in the newborn are often indistinguishable from one another.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Infectious and Parasitic Diseases — TORCH Complex
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: A hernia that cannot be reduced and has a compromised blood supply is:
questions.explanation: Strangulation is a surgical emergency causing gangrene of the contents.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A stage 1 pressure ulcer is characterised by:
questions.explanation: Stage 2 partial-thickness loss with a blister; stage 3 full-thickness skin loss; stage 4 exposure of muscle/bone.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The normal platelet count in circulating blood is approximately:

options.D: Platelets have no measurable normal range

questions.explanation: The normal platelet count is approximately 1.5 to 4 lakhs (150,000 to 400,000) per microlitre, with an average around 2.5 lakhs/microlitre, and remains quite constant under normal conditions.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: Platelets or Thrombocytes — Count and Variations
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A patient finds it easier to walk in water mainly because of:
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: an immersed body experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of water displaced, reducing weight bearing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The most important safety precaution while using a therapeutic laser is to:

options.A: Protect the eyes of the patient and operator with wavelength-specific goggles
options.B: Apply the laser to the eyes for 30 seconds
options.C: Treat in a dark, reflective room
options.D: Cover the machine with a wet towel

questions.explanation: Laser light can damage the retina even at low powers; goggles rated for the wavelength must be worn and reflective surfaces avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Early diagnosis and prompt treatment of a disease is an example of:
questions.explanation: Primordial: prevent risk factors from emerging; primary: health promotion and specific protection; secondary: early detection; tertiary: disability limitation and rehabilitation.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Insulin is secreted by the:

options.A: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans

questions.explanation: Glucagon is secreted by alpha cells; somatostatin by delta cells.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A positive straight leg raise (Lasegue) test for lumbar disc prolapse reproduces:

options.B: Pain at 90° only in the hamstrings
options.C: Radicular leg pain between about 30° and 70° of hip flexion

questions.explanation: Neural tension on the sciatic nerve roots L5/S1 typically produces leg pain before 70°; hamstring tightness gives pain at the posterior thigh only.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The definitive treatment of a mature abscess is:
questions.explanation: ‘Where there is pus, let it out’: drainage plus antibiotics where indicated.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A Timed Up and Go score greater than about 14 seconds in an older adult suggests:
questions.explanation: TUG measures time to rise from a chair, walk 3 m, turn, return and sit; >12–14 s is associated with fall risk.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Caseous necrosis is typically seen in:
questions.explanation: Cheesy white appearance with granulomatous inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The normal total serum calcium level is about:
questions.explanation: About half is ionised (active); regulated by PTH, calcitonin and vitamin D.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Infrared radiation lies in the electromagnetic spectrum:

options.A: At a shorter wavelength than ultraviolet
options.D: Between visible light and microwaves (about 700 nm to 1 mm)

questions.explanation: Infrared has longer wavelengths than visible red light. Therapeutically, 750 nm – 400,000 nm is commonly quoted.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In India, BCG vaccine is given at birth to prevent:
questions.explanation: BCG at birth (0.05 mL intradermal in the left upper arm); OPV zero dose at birth; Hepatitis B birth dose.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Therapeutic ultrasound is produced by the:

options.A: Reverse piezoelectric effect in a crystal

questions.explanation: An alternating voltage applied to a piezoelectric crystal (quartz, barium titanate, lead zirconate titanate) makes it vibrate at the same frequency, producing sound waves.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A patient with abdominal incision should support the wound during coughing by:

options.C: Holding a pillow or hands firmly over the wound (splinting)

questions.explanation: Splinting reduces pain and increases cough effectiveness; adequate analgesia is also important.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A pregnant woman with a history of four or more previous births is termed:
questions.explanation: A woman with a previous history of four or more births is called a grand multipara — distinct from nullipara (never completed a pregnancy to viability) and primipara (has delivered exactly one viable child).
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: How many carpal bones make up the wrist, and in how many rows are they arranged?
questions.explanation: The carpus is made up of 8 carpal bones arranged in two rows of four: a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, from lateral to medial) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Carpal Bones
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: During a generalised tonic–clonic seizure, the physiotherapist should:

options.A: Hold the limbs firmly to stop the jerking
options.C: Place a spoon between the teeth
options.D: Protect the head, loosen tight clothing, turn the patient to the side afterwards and not put anything in the mouth

questions.explanation: Maintain the airway, time the seizure and seek help if >5 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In long-standing rheumatoid arthritis of the hand, the fingers typically show:

options.B: Ulnar deviation at the metacarpophalangeal joints

questions.explanation: Synovitis stretches the radial collateral structures and extensor tendons subluxe ulnarward. Heberden's nodes are of osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: According to Newton's second law, force equals:
questions.explanation: F = m × a; the unit of force is the newton (kg·m/s²).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A gait with short, rapid, shuffling steps and a flexed trunk is called:
questions.explanation: Festination is characteristic of Parkinson's disease; the patient tends to hurry forward to catch up with the displaced centre of gravity.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The correct technique for lifting a heavy object from the floor is to:

options.A: Bend the back with straight legs
options.B: Bend the knees, keep the back straight and hold the load close to the body
options.D: Hold the load at arm's length

questions.explanation: Reduce lumbar load by using leg muscles and keeping the load close.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A normal arterial oxygen saturation is approximately:
questions.explanation: Below 90% indicates hypoxaemia; COPD targets are usually 88–92%.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The pathognomonic (definite) sign of a fracture is:
questions.explanation: Pain, swelling and tenderness are common but non-specific. Crepitus and abnormal mobility are definitive but should not be deliberately elicited.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Iron-deficiency anaemia typically shows:

options.C: Microcytic hypochromic red cells with low ferritin

questions.explanation: Causes: blood loss, poor intake; look for GI bleeding in men and postmenopausal women.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The earliest and most important clinical sign of impending Volkmann's ischaemic contracture after a supracondylar fracture is:

options.B: Pain on passive extension of the fingers

questions.explanation: Severe, increasing forearm pain aggravated by passive finger extension indicates ischaemia of the deep flexor compartment. Pulse loss is a late sign; claw deformity is the established contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The puerperium is the period of:

options.A: About 6 weeks after delivery during which the reproductive organs return to the non-pregnant state

questions.explanation: Involution of the uterus; lochia lasts up to 4–6 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The classical triad of bacterial meningitis is:
questions.explanation: Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs are positive; urgent lumbar puncture unless contraindicated.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Inanimate objects such as door handles, water taps, and ultrasound probes that bridge transmission of infection between hosts are called:
questions.explanation: Fomites are inanimate objects (door handles, water taps, medical equipment) that can bridge transmission of infection between an infected source and a susceptible host, and are particularly associated with health care-associated infection. Vectors, by contrast, are animate carriers (e.g. mosquitoes, fleas).
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Epidemiology of Infection — Transmission of Infection
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: A movement performed entirely by an external force with no voluntary muscle contraction by the patient is:
questions.explanation: Passive movements maintain joint range and soft tissue extensibility when the patient cannot move; they do not strengthen muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Glyceryl trinitrate relieves angina mainly by:

options.D: Venodilatation reducing preload and myocardial oxygen demand

questions.explanation: Release of nitric oxide; headache is a common side effect.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: The FIRST step in managing a patient or colleague who is still in contact with a live electrical source is to:

options.A: Wait for the person to let go on their own
options.C: Switch off the supply at the mains (or safely break contact with a non-conducting object)
options.D: Pull the person away with bare hands

questions.explanation: Touching a victim still in contact would pass current to the rescuer. Isolate the supply first, then assess breathing/circulation and start CPR if needed.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In the immediate management of acute soft tissue injury, RICE stands for:
questions.explanation: RICE limits bleeding and oedema. Many protocols now add Protection and avoid anti-inflammatory heat in the first 48–72 hours.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The commonest site of ectopic pregnancy is the:
questions.explanation: Classic triad: amenorrhoea, abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The drug used sublingually for the relief of an acute angina attack is:
questions.explanation: GTN dilates veins and coronary arteries; patients should carry it during exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: After median sternotomy for CABG, patients should AVOID:

options.C: Pushing or pulling with the arms, lifting heavy objects and unsupported coughing

questions.explanation: Sternal precautions for about 6–12 weeks prevent sternal instability: hugging a pillow when coughing, no lifting >2–5 kg, avoid pushing up with the arms.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Therapeutic ultrasound should NOT be applied over:

options.A: A chronic tendinopathy of the supraspinatus
options.B: A healing ligament sprain in the subacute phase
options.C: A muscle contracture with intact sensation
options.D: A pregnant uterus, the eyes, or a known malignant tumour

questions.explanation: Ultrasound is contraindicated over the pregnant uterus, eyes, testes, malignancy, thrombophlebitis and areas of impaired circulation or sensation; also with caution over growing epiphyses and pacemakers.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Cerebral palsy is best defined as:

options.A: A non-progressive disorder of movement and posture due to a lesion in the developing brain
options.D: A disease of the peripheral nerves

questions.explanation: The brain lesion is static but clinical manifestations evolve with growth.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which type of isolation requires only the use of a mask?
questions.explanation: Droplet precautions use a mask; contact precautions use gloves and gowns; strict isolation uses all barrier methods.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia is:
questions.explanation: Lobar consolidation with rusty sputum.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Caseous necrosis, with its characteristic 'cheese-like' gross appearance, is classically found in the centre of which type of lesion?
questions.explanation: Caseous necrosis is found classically in the centre of tuberculous foci — combining features of both coagulative and liquefactive necrosis — with surrounding granulomatous inflammation (epithelioid cells, Langhans' giant cells, and a peripheral lymphocyte mantle).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Cell Injury, Cellular Adaptations and Cellular Ageing — Caseous Necrosis
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: A well-known phenomenon in MS in which symptoms transiently worsen with rise in body temperature is called:
questions.explanation: Heat slows conduction in demyelinated axons; avoid overheating (hot baths, vigorous exercise in hot rooms) and use cooling strategies.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In a supine patient, the area most prone to pressure injury is the:
questions.explanation: Supine: occiput, scapulae, sacrum and heels; side-lying: greater trochanter and malleoli; prone: ASIS, patella and toes.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The commonest cause of COPD is:
questions.explanation: Smoking cessation is the only intervention that slows decline in FEV1.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The resting membrane potential of a typical peripheral nerve fibre is about:
questions.explanation: At rest the inside of a nerve fibre is about 70 mV negative relative to the outside. Skeletal muscle fibres rest nearer −90 mV.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The sciatic nerve divides into the tibial and common peroneal nerves at about the:

options.C: Upper angle of the popliteal fossa

questions.explanation: It leaves the pelvis via the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Bell's palsy affects the:

options.C: Facial nerve (lower motor neurone) causing unilateral facial weakness including the forehead

questions.explanation: LMN facial palsy paralyses the upper and lower face; UMN lesions spare the forehead because of bilateral cortical innervation.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The correct order of soft tissue healing is:
questions.explanation: Inflammatory (days 0–5), repair/proliferation (days 4–21) and remodelling (21 days to 1+ years).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The resting membrane potential is conventionally written with a minus sign because:

options.A: It signifies the inside of the cell is negative relative to the outside
options.B: It signifies the outside of the cell is negative relative to the inside
options.C: The sign is arbitrary and carries no physiological meaning
options.D: It indicates the cell is in the process of depolarising

questions.explanation: The resting membrane potential is written with a minus sign to indicate that, at rest, the interior of the cell is electrically negative relative to the exterior — its magnitude varies by tissue, typically ranging from about -10 mV to -100 mV.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: The Membrane Potentials — Resting Membrane Potential
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: In India, the elderly are conventionally defined as persons aged:
questions.explanation: Census and the National Policy for Older Persons use 60+; WHO uses 65 in developed countries.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A positive Thompson (Simmonds) test, with no plantar flexion on squeezing the calf, indicates:

options.D: A complete rupture of the Achilles tendon

questions.explanation: Squeezing the calf normally produces plantar flexion; absence indicates a ruptured Achilles tendon, often with a palpable gap.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Lipofuscin, sometimes called the 'wear and tear pigment', is most characteristically associated with:

options.B: Atrophied cells in ageing (e.g. 'brown atrophy' of the heart)

questions.explanation: Lipofuscin is a golden-brown intralysosomal pigment that accumulates in atrophied cells of old age (hence 'wear and tear pigment'), seen in myocardial fibres (producing 'brown atrophy' of the heart), hepatocytes, and neurons in senile dementia.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Cell Injury, Cellular Adaptations and Cellular Ageing — Lipofuscin
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: At rest, the cell membrane is:

options.A: Freely permeable to Na+ but impermeable to K+
options.B: Effectively impermeable (or only moderately permeable) to Na+, but freely permeable to K+ and Cl-
options.C: Equally permeable to Na+ and K+
options.D: Impermeable to all ions including K+ and Cl-

questions.explanation: At rest, the cell membrane is effectively impermeable (or only moderately permeable) to Na+, while being freely permeable to K+ and Cl- — K+ permeability is roughly 50-100 times greater than Na+ permeability, which is fundamental to the genesis of the resting membrane potential.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Which activity does NOT typically occur before 9 months of age?
questions.explanation: Neat pincer grasp develops at around 9–12 months.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Dupuytren's contracture is a fibrosis of the:
questions.explanation: Progressive thickening of the palmar aponeurosis creates nodules and cords, flexing the ring and little fingers at the MCP and PIP joints first.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Inguinal hernias in children are almost always caused by:

options.A: A direct defect in the abdominal wall muscles

questions.explanation: Inguinal hernias in children are almost always indirect, caused by failure of the processus vaginalis (the tongue of peritoneum that precedes testicular descent) to obliterate after birth.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — Inguinal Hernias
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The hip joint is a:
questions.explanation: Triaxial; movements: flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A proper warm-up before exercise helps by:

options.D: Increasing muscle temperature, blood flow and joint lubrication

questions.explanation: 5–10 minutes of low-intensity activity increases nerve conduction and prepares muscles for loading.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Ipsilateral motor paralysis with contralateral loss of pain and temperature below the lesion indicates:
questions.explanation: Corticospinal and dorsal column signs are ipsilateral (crossed in medulla); spinothalamic fibres cross at the segment so loss is contralateral.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Positioning of a burn patient to prevent contractures should be:

options.B: Maintained consistently throughout the day with splinting as needed

questions.explanation: Anti-deformity positioning: axilla abducted, elbow extended, neck extended, hands in the intrinsic-plus position.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In Maitland's mobilisation scale, Grade IV movement is:

options.A: A small-amplitude movement at the beginning of the range
options.B: A large-amplitude movement within the range
options.D: A small-amplitude oscillation at the end of the available range

questions.explanation: Grades I–II: smaller/larger amplitude in the first half of range (pain relief). Grades III–IV: into resistance, large (III) or small (IV) amplitude to stretch. Grade V: manipulation (thrust).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The normal end-feel at the end of elbow flexion with bulky biceps (soft tissue approximation) is:
questions.explanation: Soft end-feel = approximation of soft tissue (knee/elbow flexion). Hard = bone on bone (elbow extension); firm = capsule/ligament stretch (shoulder lateral rotation).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle occurs in the:
questions.explanation: It oxidises acetyl-CoA to CO₂, generating NADH and FADH₂.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Unintentional weight loss of more than what percentage of body weight over the preceding 6 months is considered a good indicator of poor prognosis?

options.D: Weight loss is never prognostically significant

questions.explanation: Unintentional weight loss of more than 10% of a patient's body weight over the preceding 6 months is considered a good prognostic indicator of poor outcome.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Nutritional Assessment — Body Weight and Anthropometry
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Body mass index is calculated as:

options.A: Weight in kg divided by height in metres
options.D: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared

questions.explanation: WHO classification: overweight 25–29.9, obese ≥30; Asian cut-offs are lower (23 and 25).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The axillary nerve supplies the:
questions.explanation: Arises from the posterior cord (C5–C6); sensory to the regimental badge area.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The commonest type of stroke is:
questions.explanation: About 85% of strokes are ischaemic; CT head distinguishes.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The normal active range of shoulder flexion (AAOS) is approximately:
questions.explanation: AAOS norms: shoulder flexion 0–180°, abduction 0–180°, extension 0–60°, medial rotation 0–70°, lateral rotation 0–90°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A Colles' fracture is a fracture of the:

options.B: Distal end of the radius with dorsal displacement

questions.explanation: Colles' fracture: extra-articular fracture of the distal radius (within 2.5 cm of the wrist) with dorsal angulation — the ‘dinner-fork’ deformity. Volar displacement is Smith's fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: On the Oxford/MRC scale a muscle that can move the part through full range actively but only with gravity eliminated is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 2: full range gravity-eliminated. Grade 3: full range against gravity. Grade 1: palpable contraction only. Grade 0: no contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A patient shows a visible or palpable contraction of a muscle but no joint movement. The grade is:
questions.explanation: A flicker of contraction without movement is grade 1 (Trace).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The principle of postural drainage is to:

options.B: Position the patient so the affected bronchopulmonary segment is uppermost, allowing gravity to assist secretion drainage
options.C: Place the affected segment lowest to increase perfusion
options.D: Make the patient lie supine for all segments

questions.explanation: The segmental bronchus is positioned vertically with the segment above it so secretions drain toward the larger airways, helped by percussion, vibration and coughing.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Rifampicin causes:

options.D: Orange-red discolouration of urine and other body fluids

questions.explanation: It is a potent enzyme inducer.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: An umbilical hernia in an infant, caused by incomplete closure of the umbilical ring, most commonly:

options.B: Resolves spontaneously by around 4 years of age
options.C: Always requires surgical repair within the first month of life
options.D: Is a surgical emergency due to a very high incarceration rate

questions.explanation: Umbilical hernias are common in infants and most resolve spontaneously by around 4 years of age, with incarceration being very rare — unlike supraumbilical hernias, which do not close on their own and are repaired around the same age.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — Midline Hernias
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A footballer twists his knee, hears a pop and develops immediate swelling within hours. The most likely injured structure is the:
questions.explanation: Rapid haemarthrosis after a twisting injury strongly suggests an ACL tear; meniscal injuries produce delayed effusion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A positive Babinski sign (extensor plantar response) in an adult indicates:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexion of the great toe with fanning of the other toes after stroking the lateral sole signifies pyramidal tract disease (normal in infants under about 1 year).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills
